destination.name: Vondelkerk
destination.address: Vondelstraat 120, 1054 GS Amsterdam (PDOK locatieserver: Vondelstraat 120A centroid 4.87394, 52.36130)
destination.note: No existing POI or installed model covered this pand (checked manualCatalogue.json, landmarks.json, click-poi-info.json).

facts: Neo-Gothic cross basilica (kruisbasiliek) by Pierre Cuypers; first stone 1 March 1872, completed and opened 16 June 1880 as R.K. Church of the Sacred Heart.
Octagonal crossing tower is the main tower; about 50 m high (wooden tower on a steel structure).
Fire 8 Nov 1904 destroyed the wooden tower and roof; tower rebuilt slightly lower by Joseph Cuypers (finished 1906).
Deconsecrated 1977; later concert hall, wedding venue, offices.

Fire on New Year's night 2026: the main tower and surrounding roof collapsed, walls largely stood. The model deliberately shows the pre-fire church (the 3DBAG/AHN data, municipal panoramas of 2025 and all reference photographs predate the fire).

measuredBy.3dbag: NL.IMBAG.Pand.0363100012236196, LoD2.2: nave ridge 22.3 m, 60 degree planes, eave about 12.8 m, ring 175 vertices; the crossing tower is truncated at 36.1 m and the facade towers are absent, so the church is built from its own axis frame, not from the shell.
measuredBy.axisFrame: nave axis bearing 66 degrees, origin (-4.147, 1.327) native m from the BAG centroid (4.8737838, 52.3612955); aisles +-7.15 m, nave +-5.3 m, facade plane at a=-23.2, apse tip a=19.7, transept ends b=+-14.05.
measuredBy.facadeHeights: Measured from ref-west-2007.jpg using the nave eave (12.8 m) as scale: portal arch 6.0 m, stone hood apex 9.6, triple lancet 8.0-12.4, corbel frieze 14.9, gable 15.4-19.3, tower plinth 6.8, belfry 17.3-20.1, cone tip 26.7. Crossing tower ratios from ref-east-tower-crop.jpg: belfry 27-38 m, spire tip about 47 m.
uncertain: Exact crossing-tower stage heights (single oblique photograph; +-2 m).
Transept/chancel window counts and the chapel roof shapes were read from two panoramas and one park photograph; the east apse photograph is not square-on.
Facade towers are drawn as octagons; the photographs read as octagonal tapering shafts but a round section is not excluded.
